gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the same invalid inference: fixed-radius mesh refinement is claimed to produce exact whole-space eigenvalues, although it only removes discretization and coefficient-approximation errors and leaves finite-radius Dirichlet truncation and the lower-bound Neumann correction. Both also identify that an additional R→∞ limit is required.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The h→0 limit at fixed truncation radius R converges to finite-radius bounds, not to the whole-space eigenvalue lambda_k; finite-R truncation and the fixed exterior correction remain, so exact convergence requires R→∞ as well.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed fixed-R mesh-refinement convergence to the whole-space eigenvalue is false: refinement reaches finite-radius Dirichlet and Neumann-based endpoints, with finite-R truncation and the exterior correction remaining; exact convergence requires R→∞.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states the fixed-R limiting endpoints, identifies the nonvanishing truncation gap and Neumann factor, and supplies the required additional R→∞ limit and corrected convergence statement.
